'''Wan Sandage''' was a [[Devlikk]] [[Podracer (profession)|podracer]] from the [[planet]] [[Ord Radama]] who participated in the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing|podrace]] on the [[planet]] [[Tatooine]] in [[32 BBY]]. Using a [[Wan Sandage's Podracer|vehicle]] with [[TurboDyne 99-U]] [[Podracer engine|engines]], he started in the last row of the starting grid and hung at the back of the pack once the race begun.

Sandage was the first [[pilot]] overtaken by the [[human]] [[Anakin Skywalker]], but eventually overtook his competitor [[Neva Kee]] before crashing into a [[sandcrawler]] off course during the third lap and ending up in the [[Mos Espa medcenter|Mos Espa medical center]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|I see the contestants are making their way out on to the starting grid.|Fodesinbeed Annodue commentating on Wan Sandage and the other podracers before the Boonta Eve Classic|audio=Fode-StartingGrid.flac|<ref name="TPM" />}}
[[File:TurboDyne99-U-CT.png|thumb|left|300px|Wan Sandage flew a Podracer with TurboDyne 99-U engines.]]
Wan Sandage was a [[Devlikk]] [[Podracer (profession)|podracer]] from the remote [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]] [[planet]] [[Ord Radama]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> In [[32 BBY]],<ref name="Timelines">''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the events of {{Film|I}} to [[32 BBY]].</ref> he participated in the [[Boonta Eve Classic]] [[Podracing|podrace]] on the [[desert]] [[planet]] [[Tatooine]]. As one of the less skilled participants, little was known about him at the [[time]].<ref name="Geektionary" /> The Devlikk's [[Wan Sandage's Podracer|podracer]] was pulled out onto the starting grid at the [[Mos Espa Grand Arena]] by a [[ronto]], with Sandage starting in the farside position on the fifth and final row. A [[human]] carried Sandage's flag in the procession across the grid before the race began, with the [[Troig]] [[Fodesinbeed Annodue]] providing commentary on the racers.<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>

Once [[crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] signalled the start of the race, Sandage left the grid with the other racers, but remained at the back of the pack. He was the first competitor to be overtaken by the [[human]] racer [[Anakin Skywalker]] after Skywalker initially had [[620C racing engine|engine]] trouble that prevented him from leaving the grid.<ref name="TPM" /> Sandage at some point overtook the racer [[Neva Kee]] and left him in last place before completing his second lap,<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> but in the middle of third lap,<ref name="Super">''[[Star Wars Super Graphic: A Visual Guide to a Galaxy Far, Far Away]]''</ref> Sandage flew off-course and collided with a [[Jawa]] [[sandcrawler]], resulting in him failing to complete the race.<ref name="CL 2016">[[Star Wars: Complete Locations (2016)|''Star Wars: Complete Locations'']]</ref> Sandage ended up in the [[Mos Espa medcenter|medical center]] in the [[city]] of [[Mos Espa]], where he was soon joined by fellow pilots [[Dud Bolt]] and [[Ark Roose]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

==Personality and traits==
Sandage was not a very good podracer.<ref name="Geektionary" /> He had [[Color|green]] [[hair]], tan skin, and red [[eye]]s.<ref name="Encyclopedia" />

==Equipment==
During the Boonta Eve Classic, Sandage flew a podracer with [[TurboDyne 99-U]] [[Podracer engine|engines]] that were green and tan in color.<ref name="CV">[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]]</ref> The Devlikk's flag consisted of a large rectangular yellow flag with a thin tapered white flag both above and below it.<ref name="CL 2016" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:SandageConcept-EPIGuide.png|thumb|right|300px|Concept art of Wan Sandage]]
Wan Sandage was created for the [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']],<ref name="TPM" /> which released on [[May 19]], [[1999]].<ref name="YbY">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref> Concept art of Sandage was created by [[Terryl Whitlatch]], who created a colored orthographic diagram of the Devlikk on [[September 9]], [[1996]] and a sketch of Sandage's head and face on [[November 7]] that year. Concept art of different headgear and neckwear for Sandage including goggles and an eyepatch were also created.<ref name="Guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']]</ref> The film's art department crafted a detailed maquette of Sandage with an elaborate paint scheme, but as the character is not seen close-up in the film, [[Industrial Light & Magic]] only created a fairly low-resolution digital model of Sandage to be used in distant shots<ref name="DB">{{DB|character|wansandage|Sandage, Wan}}</ref> were the Devlikk is visible in the cockpit of his vehicle.<ref name="TPM" />

The name Sandage originally appeared as [[Count]] [[Sandage]] in [[George Lucas]]' [[The Star Wars rough draft|rough]]<ref name="Rough">[[The Star Wars rough draft|''The Star Wars'' rough draft]]</ref> and [[The Star Wars first draft|first drafts]]<ref name="First">[[The Star Wars first draft|''The Star Wars'' first draft]]</ref> of the [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film, [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], although the character did not make it into the final version of the film.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> The name Wan Sandage then appears as early as Lucas's revised rough draft of the script for ''The Phantom Menace'', which listed his homeworld as [[Umboo]] rather than Ord Radama.<ref name="Guide" /> In the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]], the name was first used in "Sebulba and Rival Pilots," and article published in the "[[Weapons & Uniforms]]" department of [[Star Wars Helmet Collection 17|''Star Wars Helmet Collection'' 17]], a magazine published by [[De Agostini]]<ref name="HC17">{{HelmetCollectionCite|17|Weapons & Uniforms}}</ref> on [[August 24]], [[2016]].<ref name="Date">{{HCdates|17}}</ref> In the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, Sandage appeared prior to the release of the film in its [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|novelization]] by [[Terry Brooks]],<ref name="Novelization">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' novelization]]</ref> which was released on [[May 3]], 1999.<ref name="Insider43">[[Star Wars Insider 43|''Star Wars Insider'' 43]]</ref>
